results.draft_locus: Three Places to Keep the Engine ¶1
results.finding: Outliner marked two ideas (design one / Stripe decoupling billing from processing); the spec's p30 evidence intends the separability fact inside the description of design one. The dangling Metronome sentence is recorded under evidence_is_explained.
Every unit traces to S1-S6; intro context (p03) supports S1, scene supports S6, Stripe/Adyen sections S3/S4/S5, designs and failures S6.

results.draft_locus: Adyen's Recurring Model: A Token and a Flag ¶2
results.quote: And Adyen itself wrote, in a knowledge-hub article of 29 September 2026 on why it acquired Orb, that billing by seat and by month "is well-served today, including by partners we work with closely".
results.finding: The Auto Rescue quote is followed by what it shows, but the Orb gateway quote and this Adyen quote end the paragraph with no sentence saying what they show (spec: billing systems treat Adyen as the gateway below them, and Adyen describes that arrangement itself).

results.draft_locus: Three Places to Keep the Engine ¶1

results.draft_locus: Stripe and Adyen: Where They Differ ¶1
results.quote: The table sets the two companies side by side. Each Stripe and Adyen cell repeats a fact cited above; the last column is my inference.

results.draft_locus: What to Take Away ¶3
results.finding: States what no section states (scheduler, calculator and state machine as three views of one answer, failures as that answer late, doubled or under the wrong rule) and gives the so-what as a course of action (one line per decision with its system and read-back).

results.draft_locus: What to Take Away ¶3
results.quote: The 1,840 members who paid for November twice were missing exactly that record.
results.finding: Explicit callback to the opening incident (spec callback.to).

The intro reader predicted all nine body sections in the roadmap's order, the evidence (dated vendor documentation, fictional Larkfield case) and the tone. Unclear only on what 'three places' are and on whether 'ways billing goes wrong' equals the three callout patterns (the section uses late/twice/wrong rule/wrong state).

The cold reader named the day (month-end rule), the instant/time zone, proration value and now-vs-next-invoice, status and access while unpaid, and a per-period record with a derived idempotency key; all expected decisions present, plus pacing.

The cold reader stated that Adyen provides a stored token and a merchant-initiated payment flagged Subscription; schedule, amount, proration, invoice and state live with the merchant or a connected billing system; Orb closed 1 July 2026, runs separately, no integrated product documented as of November 2026.

Every statement on Stripe's scheduler or Adyen's platform is cited with date (n.d., accessed November 2026, or publication date) or labeled (two INFERENCE, NOT DOCUMENTED blocks, 'I conclude ... inference from absence', the comparison table's inference column). Stripe ¶7 and the comparison table say where the record stops: one 2024 engineering post describes a scanning scheduling service; partitioning, pacing and duplicate protection are not public; Adyen documents no first-party scheduler.
